intro: Brač's protected tree is an oddity rather than an ancient. In the inland village of Nerežišća, a pine about 170 centimetres tall grows out of the roof of the church of St Peter and Paul, with no roots found reaching the ground. Officials estimate it at about 120 years, with uncertainty, and Croatia declared it a natural monument in 1969 as a rare specimen. It is seen from the street, so the church need not be open.
meta_description: The pine on the church roof in Nerežišća, Brač: about 170 cm tall, around 120 years by an official guess, protected since 1969.
question_meta: Brač's best-known tree is a pine growing from the roof of the church of St Peter and Paul in Nerežišća.
question_answer: Brač's best-known tree is the pine on the roof of the church of St Peter and Paul in Nerežišća, about 170 centimetres tall and protected as a natural monument since 1969. Officials estimate it at about 120 years, and say they are not sure.
question_context: The pine is the draw because of where it grows, not its size or age. Total Croatia News reported in 2017 that it stands 170 centimetres tall on the roof of the church of St Peter and Paul, that no roots have been found reaching the ground, and that it lives on rainwater. Officials put it at about 120 years with uncertainty. One island guide identifies it as a miniature black pine. The church itself is given as about 600 years old by Total Croatia News, and as 13th or 14th century by other sources. Croatia protected the tree in 1969 as a rare specimen. Nerežišća lies inland, reached from the ferry port at Supetar by island bus or car, and the roof is visible from the street in the village centre, so there are no opening hours to worry about. The most recent dated report of the pine that we found is from 2017, so a visitor who sees it now knows more than we do.

faq.q: Where is the tree on the church roof on Brač?
faq.a: On the church of St Peter and Paul in the centre of Nerežišća, an inland village reached from Supetar. It is seen from the street.

faq.q: How old is the Nerežišća roof pine?
faq.a: About 120 years by an official estimate that admits its uncertainty. It is about 170 centimetres tall.

trees.story:
A pine grows out of the roof of the church in Nerežišća, and nobody has found its roots reaching the ground. By Total Croatia News' account in 2017, it lives on rainwater.

It is 170 centimetres tall, about the height of a person, on the church of St Peter and Paul in the centre of this inland village on Brač. Total Croatia News puts the church at about 600 years old; other sources place it in the 13th or 14th century. Officials estimate the pine at about 120 years, and say plainly that they are not sure. One island guide calls it a miniature black pine, and an English Wikipedia caption simply shows the chapel with its bonsai tree.

Croatia declared it a natural monument in 1969 as a rare specimen. This is not an ancient tree and it does not need to be. It is an oddity, a pine put at over a century old by the official guess and still shorter than most of the people who stop to look at it, and the village has kept it.

You do not need the church open to see it. The roof is visible from the street in the village centre, and Nerežišća is a short trip inland from the ferry port at Supetar.

The most recent dated report we found is from 2017. If you pass through, look up and tell us whether it is still there.
